title: 15+10 · you White · Alapin
logNote: Stopped at a6; missed Bd7 Bxg2 e6. Red1 is pseudo-activity vs Rfd8.

steps.name: 1 Three ply
steps.title: After 19…Qa5, White to move
steps.prompt: You looked at 20.a4 and did not play it. Name the reply that stopped you, then keep going past it.

mixups.key: That skips 21.Bd7. Without …a6 and Bd7 first, …Bxg2 is just a loose capture: 21.Kxg2 and White is winning (~+5). Same capture, different position.
Recapture first and …Qd5+ forks the king and d7. It stays roughly level, but you are the one scrambling. 22.e6 comes first — the in-between move this dossier is named after.

steps.key: …a6 is ply 1, not the end. 21.Bd7 Bxg2 22.e6! and it is level. The reply you disliked was not a refutation.

steps.name: 2 Diagnose
steps.title: After 19…Qa5, White to move
steps.prompt: Candidates only. Do not stop at the first reply you dislike.

questions.name: material
questions.label: 2.1 Material
questions.hint: Who is up, and by how much?

steps.key:
Material: Black a pawn up. The minus is also the queen on a5 and the bishops vs uncoordinated White.

If you stopped at …a6, that is the leak. Next step is the line past a6 — not Red1.

steps.name: 3 Calculate
steps.title: Four lines. Same capture is not the same eval.
steps.prompt: Open a branch. Play the moves on the board. Lock that branch. The step's key opens once all four are locked.

questions.name: retreats
questions.label: After 20.a4 a6, three legal squares that keep Bb5

questions.name: zwischen
questions.label: After 21…Bxg2, e6 or Kxg2 — and why?

questions.name: bd4q
questions.label: Bd4 …Qxa2 — is the queen trapped like in the game?

branches.label: a4 a6 Bd7 Bxg2 e6
branches.key: The skipped line. 21.Bd7 keeps the bishop (Bc4, Bd3 also). 21…Bxg2 is the shot — not a reason to reject a4. 22.e6! zwischenzug, do not recapture first. ≈ equal.

branches.label: a4 Bxg2?? (no Bd7)
branches.key: Same capture, opposite eval. Without a6/Bd7, 21.Kxg2 and White is winning (~+5). Do not mix this with the Bd7 line.

branches.label: Bd4 Qxa2
branches.key: Looks central, drops a2. Bishop left b2, so Ra1 does not trap the queen. ~−3.

branches.label: Red1 Rfd8
branches.key: Pseudo-activity. The rook looks busy. Black contests the file and you are worse (~−1.7). This is the move if he does not grab a2.

steps.key: All four. a4 is not refuted by a6. Bxg2 with Bd7 is a fight; Bxg2 without Bd7 is a blunder. Bd4 loses a2. Red1 dies to Rfd8.

steps.name: 4 Trap
steps.title: The game: after 20.Red1, Black to move

questions.name: instead
questions.label: The move that refutes Red1 if Black does not grab?

steps.key: 21.Ra1, then 22.Ra3. Refutation if he does not grab: …Rfd8.

steps.name: 5 Hunt
steps.title: After 21…Qb3, White to move
steps.prompt: Play the hunt move, then tag the game honestly.

options.label: I calculated the trap and he walked in
He hung it; 20.Red1 was still a mistake
Both: the hunt was real, and Red1 still needed the blunder

steps.key: Tag calculation, not clean. The miss was stopping at …a6. Logged to the dossier.
